title: Rentosertib, a drug designed with generative AI, improves lung function in a phase 2a trial for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and a phase 3 trial begins in China
summary: Rentosertib, designed with Insilico Medicine's generative-AI platform, raised mean forced vital capacity by 98.4 mL at 60 mg daily in a phase 2a trial, against a fall of 20.3 mL on placebo.
account: Rentosertib, a TNIK inhibitor designed with Insilico Medicine's generative-AI platform, was tested in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2a trial (NCT05938920). The authors report that the trial enrolled 71 patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis at 21 sites in China from 19 July 2023 to 11 June 2024. The registry lists 22 locations, a start date of 19 June 2023 and study completion on 8 August 2024. The primary endpoint was safety. Treatment-emergent adverse events were similar across arms. Patients on 60 mg once daily showed a mean forced vital capacity change of +98.4 mL versus -20.3 mL on placebo over 12 weeks. In the 60 mg group, 12 of the 18 patients completed the 12-week period. Insilico sponsored the trial. Eleven authors are its employees, and the first author is at Peking Union Medical College Hospital. Results appeared in Nature Medicine on 3 June 2025. The authors call for larger, longer trials. On 11 May 2026 the authors of an independent network meta-analysis reported a non-significant trend toward a higher risk of serious adverse events with rentosertib than with placebo. On 7 July 2026 Insilico announced that it was initiating a phase 3 trial. The registry lists 9 September 2026 as the actual start date of GENESIS-IPF-3, a 52-week phase 3 trial at Chinese hospitals, and plans for 320 participants. On 10 September 2026 Insilico announced that it had dosed the first patient, and it stated that the drug has no regulatory approval.
purpose: Rentosertib was designed as an antifibrotic treatment for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The trial tested the safety and preliminary efficacy of exactly that intended benefit.
system: Insilico Medicine generative-AI drug discovery platform (target discovery and generative chemistry) that produced rentosertib (ISM001-055)
model_version: PandaOmics (Biology42) and Chemistry42, Insilico Pharma.AI platform
deployer: Insilico Medicine (trial sponsor) with 21 clinical centers in China

ratings.reason: Patients on 60 mg once daily gained a mean 98.4 mL in forced vital capacity over 12 weeks, while patients on placebo lost 20.3 mL. This is a measured improvement in a lung function test, which was a secondary endpoint in a small trial. Three patients on 60 mg and one on placebo had an acute exacerbation, and no lasting change in any patient's disease is reported.
Any wider benefit depends on confirmation in larger, longer trials, which the authors say are warranted. The phase 3 trial began dosing in September 2026 and has no results.

ai_role.statement: The AI role is upstream: generative-AI tools identified TNIK as a target and designed the molecule. Any clinical effect is pharmacological. The trial was not powered for efficacy and FVC was not the primary endpoint. An independent network meta-analysis ranks rentosertib favorably on FVC decline but reports a non-significant trend toward more serious adverse events.

fields.summary: Rentosertib, designed with Insilico Medicine's generative-AI platform, raised mean forced vital capacity by 98.4 mL at 60 mg daily in a phase 2a trial, against a fall of 20.3 mL on placebo.
fields.account: Rentosertib, a TNIK inhibitor designed with Insilico Medicine's generative-AI platform, was tested in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2a trial (NCT05938920). The authors report that the trial enrolled 71 patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis at 21 sites in China from 19 July 2023 to 11 June 2024. The registry lists 22 locations, a start date of 19 June 2023 and study completion on 8 August 2024. The primary endpoint was safety. Treatment-emergent adverse events were similar across arms. Patients on 60 mg once daily showed a mean forced vital capacity change of +98.4 mL versus -20.3 mL on placebo over 12 weeks. In the 60 mg group, 12 of the 18 patients completed the 12-week period. Insilico sponsored the trial. Eleven authors are its employees, and the first author is at Peking Union Medical College Hospital. Results appeared in Nature Medicine on 3 June 2025. The authors call for larger, longer trials. On 11 May 2026 the authors of an independent network meta-analysis reported a non-significant trend toward a higher risk of serious adverse events with rentosertib than with placebo. On 7 July 2026 Insilico announced that it was initiating a phase 3 trial. The registry lists 9 September 2026 as the actual start date of GENESIS-IPF-3, a 52-week phase 3 trial at Chinese hospitals, and plans for 320 participants. On 10 September 2026 Insilico announced that it had dosed the first patient, and it stated that the drug has no regulatory approval.
